clue.text: Tricky activity, where good taste and Labour, perhaps, slip back

indicators.note: back, placed after the last piece, tells us the whole string of pieces is read from end to start

parts.note: a nip is a small taste of a drink
Labour is one example of a political party
a boob is a blunder or slip

explanation.surface: Someone wonders where refinement and the Labour Party went wrong in some devious scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns the whole run G + NIP + PARTY + BOOB, giving BOOB YTRAP PIN G. 'slip back' reads as one phrase, but 'slip' is BOOB and 'back' alone is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting hidden traps is a tricky, devious activity, since rigging one involves concealed mischief.

clue.text: Mule is turning into beast

definitions.note: a noun in the clue, a mule being a stubborn creature, standing for the adjective describing it

indicators.note: is turning says the letters of the next two words are being churned into a new order

explanation.surface: A mule is changing into some other beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is turning' signals an anagram of INTO + BEAST. 'Mule' is the definition by way of the animal's proverbial stubbornness.
explanation.definitionFit: Mules are proverbially stubborn, so a mule-like person is one who refuses to budge.

clue.text: Setter's comment about a former Israeli PM

indicators.note: about means going round, so the bark wraps around the letter

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, and a dog's comment is a bark

explanation.surface: The crossword setter makes a remark on a past Israeli prime minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' tempts you to think of Paul, the compiler, but here it is the dog. Ehud Barak was prime minister of Israel from 1999 to 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Ehud Barak led the Israeli government at the turn of the millennium, a former premier.

clue.text: Sound of fiddle in Florida

definitions.note: a place-phrase standing for the city located there

indicators.note: Sound of says we want a word that is pronounced like the next word's synonym

parts.note: to fiddle with something is to tamper with it

explanation.surface: Somewhere in Florida, someone hears a violin playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddle' looks like the violin; it is the verb, to tamper. In a non-rhotic British accent the two words are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a large city on the Gulf Coast of the state, so it lies within Florida.

clue.text: Man United playing away from home?

definitions.text: Man United playing away from home?

parts.words: Man United playing away from home?
parts.note: reads like Manchester United on an away fixture, but means a married man who is unfaithful, playing away being slang for having an affair

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man United' is the football club Manchester United; read it as a man united in marriage, and 'playing away from home' becomes cheating on a spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A married man straying from his partner is committing infidelity, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Metal suits vessel, then nothing works

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel
O looks like zero, meaning nothing
plies means works at, as in plies a trade

explanation.surface: An armourer's suits are made from a pot, then nothing operates them.
explanation.definitionFit: Panoplies are complete suits of armour, metal suits worn by knights.

clue.text: English track among Poles, this Welsh name

indicators.note: among means placed in the midst of, so the poles go either side

parts.note: N and S are the north and south poles
RY is short for railway, a track

explanation.surface: An English railway runs between the Poles, under a Welsh name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerys is a female given name of Welsh origin.

clue.text: Equips with cruelty in a slovenly manner, or a charming one

definitions.note: stands for an adverb: 'one' here means a manner, so 'in a charming manner'

indicators.note: in a slovenly manner says the letters are thrown together untidily into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone kits people out cruelly and sloppily, or else with charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a slovenly manner' rearranges EQUIPS + CRUELTY. 'or a charming one' means 'or in a charming manner', with 'one' standing in for 'manner'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something in a pretty, charming way that looks like a painting is doing it picturesquely.

clue.text: One set off after another with revolutionary, or the Incas

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests turning things over, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the plural means one Inca
and a second Inca, the plural giving two

explanation.surface: A revolutionary sets off one thing after another, as the Incas did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' signals the anagram. The fodder is OR + THE + INCA + INCA: 'Incas' as a plural supplies two of them, giving thirteen letters with no S.
explanation.definitionFit: In a chain reaction each event sets off the next, one after another.

clue.text: Promising truth about why people prefer London?

definitions.text: Promising truth about why people prefer London?

parts.words: Promising truth about why people prefer London?
parts.note: a cheeky reading of a well-known saying about the north of England being bleak, as if it explained a preference for the capital

explanation.walkthrough: The saying is a British cliché that northern England is bleak; read literally, it would be a reason to prefer living in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying expresses a stereotype that life in northern England is harsh and dreary.

clue.text: See 10
See 25
Put an end to wine, Italian for starters

parts.note: a tip is the end of something, like the tip of a finger
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: Stop the wine; the Italian is having the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put an end to wine' reads as a command to stop drinking, but it is a charade instruction. 'Italian for starters' means the Italian word for starters.
explanation.definitionFit: Antipasti is the Italian term for appetiser dishes served before the main meal.

clue.text: Many papers are, sort of, paper

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to sort or rearrange, so the word are is reordered

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a written paper

explanation.surface: Lots of newspapers are, in a way, just paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' reads as 'kind of' but means rearranging ARE into REA; MS is a manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a large quantity of paper sheets, so reams are many papers.

clue.text: Uprising hordes obscuring donkey, black, obscuring device

indicators.note: obscuring means covering, so the reversed word wraps round the donkey
in a down clue uprising means read upwards, so the word is reversed

parts.note: mobs are hordes of people
MOKE is British slang for a donkey
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Rioting crowds hide a donkey under black, using a device to block the view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uprising' turns the hordes upwards, giving SBOM, and 'obscuring' wraps that round the donkey before black is added. The second 'obscuring' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke bomb releases a cloud that hides things from view, so it is a device for obscuring.

clue.text: One in wig finding way through wall

indicators.note: through means passing into the middle, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a wall is a barrier
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Someone in a wig finds a route through a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: British barristers traditionally wear wigs in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers in British courts wear horsehair wigs, so one is a person in a wig.

clue.text: One's bananas yelling in yellow? One must be cracked!

definitions.meaning: someone wild about the Brazil football team, who play in yellow shirts, a fanatic or nut
a hard-shelled seed that has to be broken open to eat

explanation.walkthrough: Brazil's national football team play in yellow; a fanatical fan is a nut for them. The second definition is the edible seed with its tough shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brazilian supporter mad about their team would be a fan of that country, and the nut needs cracking open.

clue.text: Club managed by county's opener in the cricket side

indicators.note: in means placed inside the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
to run something is to manage it

indicators.note: opener means the first letter of the word county's

parts.note: ON is the leg side of the field in cricket

explanation.surface: A club run by a county's opening batsman on the cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the on side, or leg side, is the half of the field behind the batsman's legs. 'opener' gives C, and 'in' puts the managing and the C inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A truncheon is a short heavy club, as carried by British police.

clue.text: Ancient vegetarian I fitted into a truss, awkwardly

indicators.note: fitted into means placed within the other piece
awkwardly says the letters of a truss are jumbled

parts.note: the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: A primitive plant-eater fits itself into a truss, with difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkwardly' rearranges the letters into STSAUR, and 'fitted into' puts the self (I) inside after the first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Stegosaurs were dinosaurs that ate plants, so they were prehistoric herbivores.

clue.text: Dive off small island

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island

explanation.surface: Someone goes diving off a little island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is a link word joining definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To scuba is to dive using self-contained breathing apparatus.

clue.text: Heartless wildebeest about to eat fish in fishy feature

indicators.note: to eat means taking the next piece inside
about says the word is turned round

parts.note: a gnu is a wildebeest

indicators.note: in puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: a fin is a feature of a fish
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A callous wildebeest is about to swallow a fish in a fishy part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the wildebeest to UNG; 'in' gives FEELIN, and 'to eat' puts that inside UNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unfeeling lacks compassion, which is to be heartless.

clue.text: Blooming cheeky!

definitions.meaning: flourishing and newly flowering, in good health

explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' might seem an exclamation like 'blooming cheek', but it is a separate sense of new and flourishing.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh flowers are blooming, and a fresh remark is impertinent or cheeky.

clue.text: One instrument or another? No thanks love

indicators.note: No signals that something is removed from the word

parts.note: another instrument, a guitar
TA is British informal for thanks
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: Someone asks which instrument to play, then declines with affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' points to a second instrument, the guitar; TA, British slang for thanks, is removed, and O for love is added. A guiro is a Latin American scraped gourd.
explanation.definitionFit: A guiro is a percussion instrument made from a notched gourd scraped with a stick.

clue.text: Early Briton carrying round loops

definitions.note: plural in the clue, while the answer names a single such loop or an edging of them

indicators.note: carrying means holding something inside

parts.note: the Picts were ancient people of northern Britain
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An ancient Briton carries something round in loops.
explanation.walkthrough: The Picts were early inhabitants of Scotland; O goes inside PICT.
explanation.definitionFit: A picot is a small decorative loop of thread forming an edging on lace or ribbon.

clue.text: Harbour something of value?

parts.note: the US naval base attacked in 1941 shares its name with a precious gem from an oyster

explanation.walkthrough: Pearl Harbor is the Hawaiian naval base; the word before 'Harbor' is also a gem.
explanation.definitionFit: A pearl is a precious gem and the first word of a famous harbour's name.

clue.text: Concede song not plagiarised?

parts.note: a lied is a German art song
work that is your own is not copied from anyone

explanation.surface: A songwriter admits defeat over a song that was not copied.
explanation.walkthrough: LIED, a German art song, is common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie down is to submit or give in without a fight, conceding.

clue.text: Paul eschews intellectualism — what could be worse?

definitions.meaning: the setter, Paul, says he dislikes thought
the reply when an outcome is too dreadful to contemplate

explanation.walkthrough: Paul is the setter of this puzzle. The second definition is the idiom said when you would rather not imagine how bad things might get.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying you would rather not imagine something expresses dread at how bad it could be.

clue.text: Weaving? Here? This is most essential

definitions.meaning: Bottom is the weaver in A Midsummer Night's Dream, so lines about weaving belong to his part
the crucial point or fundamental consideration

explanation.walkthrough: Nick Bottom is the weaver in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, so talk of weaving is Bottom's line. 'This is' links to the second definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom line is the crucial, fundamental point, what matters most in the end.
